Only those elements are copied back, odd elements remain -1 on the host. The GCC parse error on the second colon is a missing feature, and a conforming 5.2 compiler must accept it.

OpenMP 5.2 allows array sections with stride in C in motion clauses of target update (new in 5.0). a[0:8:2] designates a[0],a[2],...,a[14], stride is positive. a is present from enter data, so the target region does not remap it; update from copies only even elements, odd stay -1 on the host. Check passes; a 5.2 compiler must accept the syntax.

The expected pass follows; rejecting the syntax is a compiler error.

Section 5.9 says list items of data-motion clauses may include array sections with stride expressions, and the array-section syntax allows lower-bound:length:stride. So from(a[0:8:2]) on target update is allowed in 5.2 and updates a[0], a[2], ..., a[14]. The array a is mapped by the enter data, so the update is valid. A compiler that rejects it is wrong.

Section 5.9 says the list items of the data-motion clauses may include array sections with stride expressions, and 3.2.5 defines the C syntax [lower-bound : length : stride]. a[0:8:2] covers a[0], a[2], ..., a[14] and is a subset of a[16]. a is already mapped by enter data, so the update from copies exactly those elements and the odd ones stay -1. The parser error about ':' is a missing feature, not a spec restriction.

OpenMP 5.2 3.2.5 defines the C array section syntax [lower-bound : length : stride]. Section 13.9 says target update list items may include array sections with stride expressions, which is the stated exception to the stride restriction. The program's a[0:8:2] selects elements 0,2,...,14. A conforming compiler must accept it. The parse error is a compiler bug.

Mapping a again in the target region only raises the reference count, so no transfer overwrites the host data. The program is conforming and the strided update must be accepted, so the syntax error is a compiler defect.

The update copies back only the even elements; odd ones stay -1. No race. A conforming compiler must accept the syntax.
